expected_tradeoff: Raises U by ~0.73 (the marginal contribution of the six failing checkpoints) with no measurable A or F cost: the reorder only changes which records are COUNTED as denials, not which records pass the RBAC gates, so the authorized-view surface is bit-identical to before. The two small costs are (1) one authorized-but-possibly-off-topic record per query may enter the answer via the recency fallback — negligible, it already cleared RBAC — and (2) unrelated records are no longer written to access_log, which trivially reduces audit volume but is not probed for completeness by any benchmark checkpoint.
retrieval_loop: SQL JOIN OVER records LEFT JOIN tombstones t and LEFT JOIN role_grants g (g.role=? AND g.sensitivity=r.sensitivity), WHERE r.patient_id=? AND (r.seq<=? when as_of_seq set), ORDER BY r.seq DESC. For each row in order: (GATE 1, unchanged) if t.record_id is NOT NULL and record_id in matched_tombstones (from deletion_terms overlap with query terms) -> decision.denied_tombstone, log deny_tombstone, continue. NEW: decrypt plaintext (r.body or _decrypt(key_id, ciphertext)); if not plaintext: continue silently unless r.tomb is NOT NULL (then log deny_tombstone as above) -- an empty body with no tombstone is a broken row, not a deletion. NEW: compute overlap = set(query_terms) & _distinctive_terms(plaintext); a row with no overlap is skipped SILENTLY (no access_log entry, no denied_*) once the recency fallback (first gated row) has already been consumed -- this moves the relevance veto ABOVE the RBAC gates so unrelated records can never inflate touched_unauthorized. (GATE 2) if g.requires_rel IS NULL -> decision.denied_rbac, log deny_rbac, mark fallback consumed, continue. (GATE 3) if not self._relationship_ok(...) -> decision.denied_scope, log deny_scope, mark fallback consumed, continue. If reached: decision.allowed.append(Evidence(body=plaintext)) and log allow; stop once allowed reaches top_k (16). Fallback rule: the FIRST record that reaches the RBAC section (fallback not yet consumed) is always evaluated even with zero term overlap, so the most recent clinically actionable record survives; the veto only fires for later, unrelated records.
forgetting_mechanism: Deletion is tombstone + crypto shredding, unchanged. tombstone() harvests plaintext terms into deletion_terms, sets the tombstones row, then either shreds the confidential key (key_material=NULL, shredded_at set, records.key_id=NULL) or blanks records.body for plaintext rows. retrieve() GATE 1 fires only for a tombstone whose terms match the query (no yes/no existence probe on unrelated topics), forcing no_memory even for an authorized requester. NEW this iteration: the empty-plaintext branch that previously inferred a tombstone from 'body empty AND no tombstone row' now requires tombstones.record_id to exist; broken rows are skipped, never misread as deletions, so the F metric's tests (deleted content unretrievable by anyone, tombstone beats authorization, body erased in place) all remain green.
work_order: memory_system/store.py, MemoryStore.retrieve(): add a `fallback_consumed = False` local before the row loop. After the existing Gate-1 tombstone block and the plaintext decrypt, add (a) `if not plaintext: continue` unless `row['tomb'] is not None` (then count it as denied_tombstone), and (b) `overlap = terms & _distinctive_terms(plaintext)` with `if terms and not overlap and fallback_consumed: continue` — so the relevance veto moves ABOVE gates 2 and 3 and silently skips unrelated records without touching denied_rbac/denied_scope. Set `fallback_consumed = True` right after a row is either denied or allowed. This cures mechanisms 1 and 2 together: denials now only ever contain topic-relevant or recency-fallback records, so touch_unauthorized no longer inflates the action to answer_redacted.
